newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: President's son apologises amid S.Korean scandal.
newsitem.headline: President's son apologises amid S.Korean scandal.

text.p: South Korean President Kim Young-sam's son, facing opposition charges of influence-peddling and meddling in state affairs, on Monday apologised to his father and the nation.
Kim Hyun-chul said he repented for causing trouble and anxiety, but did not mention two scandals to which his name has been linked and which are dogging his father's presidency.
The first involves billions of dollars of improper loans to failed Hanbo Steel Co and the second to claims that he played a key role in administration appointments and policy.
On Monday the trial began of a former cabinet minister, the founder of the Hanbo Group and eight other people in connection with loans to the country's second-biggest steelmaker.
"I, Kim Hyun-chul, bow deeply to the people and apologise," a statement from the president's second son said.
He has no government position but has been dubbed the "crown prince" by opposition parties, which have launched an all-out campaign to discredit him and his father in a presidential election year.
"I wanted to help my father but as a consequence made the mistake of causing trouble to father and anxiety to the people. I am deeply repentant now," the statement said.
He said he "wept profusely" when he saw his father apologise on television last month.
Kim senior apologised over the scandal involving $5.8 billion in loans to Hanbo, which folded in January. He said he felt shame that his son's name had been linked to the furore.
State prosecutors exonerated Hyun-chul in a probe into Hanbo's collapse, but the opposition slammed the investigation as a whitewash and demanded a new inquiry.

Kim Hyun-chul said he was prepared to testify before parliament and would agree to a new prosecution probe into his role in the Hanbo affair. "I will willingly accept any punishment if I was in the wrong," he said.
The trial of 10 people charged over the Hanbo collapse opened in a Seoul criminal court.
Former home affairs minister Kim Woo-suk has been charged with bribery and Hanbo founder Chung Tae-soo with fraud, issuing bad cheques and violating laws on trust and savings companies.

Also in the dock on corruption charges were three top bankers, four legislators -- three of them close Kim aides and one from the opposition -- and Chung's chief accountant, who was charged with embezzlement.
All defendants, who are now in custody, were dressed in pale blue prison uniforms with white rubber shoes.
Former minister Kim admitted taking money from Hanbo's Chung, but not as a bribe.
"I did receive money, but I thought it was innocent. I regret now receiving money. Had I not received the money I would not be here today," he said.
He said he found the money in a crate of apples placed in his car by an aide to Chung while the two were at dinner.

Last week, a videotape showing Kim Hyun-chul discussing a top media appointment fanned a national furore. Opposition parties and the media seized on the tape as solid evidence that the younger Kim meddled in state affairs.
